chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Bakr ibn Salih, from Suleyman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:

I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) saying: 'The remedy for a tooth is to take a colocynth, peel it, then extract its oil. If the tooth has a cavity, drip drops into it and place some of it in cotton and put it in the hollow of the tooth, and the owner lies down on his back; this is done for three nights. If the tooth has no cavity but has a smell, drip two or three drops into the ear adjacent to that tooth every night; he will be cured by the permission of Allah.'

He said: 'And I heard him saying: For the pain in the mouth, the blood that comes out from the teeth, the ulcers, and the redness that occurs in the mouth, take a moist colocynth that has turned yellow, place a clay mold over it, then pierce its head and insert a knife into it, gently rubbing its sides. Then pour over it strong, sour date vinegar, place it on the fire and boil it vigorously. Then the owner takes what fits under his fingernail and rubs it in his mouth, and gargles with vinegar. If he wishes, he can transfer what is in the colocynth into a glass jar or bowl. Whenever the vinegar is used up, he refills it, and the older it becomes, the better it is, if Allah wills.'

key_terms.حَنْظَلَة: Colocynth (a bitter fruit used in traditional medicine)
key_terms.ضَرَبَان: Ulcer or sore in the mouth
key_terms.ضِرْس: Tooth (specifically a molar or tooth with a cavity)

ai.seo_question: What is the prophetic remedy for toothache and mouth ulcers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) illustrates the Shia tradition of 'Tibb al-Nabi' (Prophetic Medicine), emphasizing practical, accessible remedies using natural ingredients like colocynth and date vinegar. It distinguishes between treating structural dental decay and halitosis, while also addressing oral ulcers and bleeding, reflecting the Imams' holistic approach to health that integrates spiritual trust (Tawakkul) with empirical observation.

en.hubeali: H 14680 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Bakr Bin Saleh, from Suleyman Bin Ja’far Al-Ja’fary who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hassan Musaasws saying: ‘To cure the toothache, take colocynth (a bitter fruit), peel it, then extracts its oil. So if the tooth has a cavity, apply the drops by cotton, place it inside the cavity and lie down upon the back. He should do this for three nights. And if the tooth does not have a cavity to it and it has a smell to it, apply the drops in each side of that tooth during the night. Every night two or three drops. He would be free (cured) by the Permission of Allahazwj’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘For the pain in the mouth and the blood which comes out from the teeth, and the ulcers and the redness which takes place in the mouth, take damp colocynth which has turned yellow, place it in a pot of clay, pierce its head and enter a knife inside it. Then gently rub its sides, then pour over it dates and vinegar, and it would be intensely bitter. Then place it upon the fire and boil it intensely. Then take from it all that can be carried by his finger, rub it in his mouth, and gargle with the vinegar. If he likes he can transfer what is in the colocynth into a bottle or bowl. And when all that becomes less, he can refill it with vinegar, and he would be free from all that, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
